youtube.aciklama: In dichotic listening, a word in the right ear reaches the language-dominant left hemisphere directly through the crossed pathway, while a word in the left ear must cross the corpus callosum. So the right ear is usually slightly better for verbal stimuli; Kimura first described this in 1961.

A right-ear word reaches the language-dominant left hemisphere via the crossed path.
A word in the left ear first reaches the right hemisphere.
It then crosses to the left through the corpus callosum.
So for verbal stimuli, the right ear is usually slightly better.
